According to this model, about 20.2% of students would drink zero cups,

Because we generated

should land in the same neighborhood — a real check

Close, not identical — 15.8% observed zero-cup students vs. 20.2%
theoretical, 36.7% vs. 32.3% at one cup, and so on. That gap is exactly what
you’d expect from a sample of only 120 students; a model doesn’t reproduce
its own theoretical percentages exactly every time it’s used to generate
data, and neither will a real dataset match its true population model
exactly. The overall

— most students at 0–2 cups, dropping off
fast after that — clearly matches.
